assets.name: 钢头盔
assets.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / style-transfer.
Production asset: one empty wearable STEEL HELMET sprite layer for a very low resolution 32x48 pixel character.
Image 1 is the existing helmet placement template. Image 2 is the character body FOR ALIGNMENT ONLY; never draw any body, skin, face or character pixels in the output.
Redraw the helmet from image 1 as a simple rounded open-face forged steel bowl, low domed cap with a solid reinforced brow and ONE short close-fitting rear ear guard at the far image-right side. Match the same almost frontal slightly left-facing head, size and position on the full transparent portrait canvas. The cap occupies logical x5..28,y1..12; the small rear ear guard may continue only at x24..27,y12..19. End all equipment by y19, well above the neck. The ENTIRE face opening, approximately x7..23,y12..21, must be completely transparent, with BOTH EYES, forehead, nose, cheeks and mouth of the reference body unobstructed when overlaid.
Artwork must look natively hand placed at 32x48 logical resolution, enlarged to a 1024x1536 2:3 transparent canvas without adding detail. HARD SQUARE PIXEL BLOCKS, one logical pixel=32x32 export pixels. Extremely simple coarse low-resolution silhouette. Use no more than SIX opaque flat colors: dark charcoal outline #1F252F, dark steel #323D4D, medium steel #4E5D6F, light steel #75889B, one restrained steel highlight #9FB0BF and a tiny dark brown lining #5A3A27. Each tone forms a BROAD CONNECTED REGION. The upper-left light highlight is a single compact solid patch, no thin diagonal stripes, no isolated speckles. Right half broad dark shade. Flat colors with no texture, no gradients.
Keep the whole shared character canvas and all transparent margins: do not center or zoom the cap, do not output a standalone inventory icon. Output empty equipment only on genuine alpha transparency, alpha zero in all face openings. No character, no face, no skin, no hair, no mannequin, no backplate inside face. No dangling straps, braids, chains, feathers, crest, pointed crown, horns, visor, rivets, scratches, dither, checkerboard highlights, alternating bright pixels, crosshatching, white shine, antialiasing, soft edges, glow, background or text.
assets.refinementPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target is this EMPTY STEEL HELMET wearable overlay on a 1024x1536 transparent canvas. Keep the helmet position, size, rounded bowl, brow, broad flat steel color clusters and image-right short ear guard exactly unchanged.
Fix ONLY the stray dangling fragments at the IMAGE-LEFT FRONT EDGE below the brow. Remove BOTH vertical strips on the far left underneath the brow: the short strip around x240..295,y385..465 AND the detached strip around x265..295,y510..595. Make all of x0..310,y380..650 fully alpha zero. This left front side must end cleanly at the solid horizontal brow, without any hanging straps, vertical bars or isolated pixels. The body face will show through this area later; do not draw a face.
Maintain a crisp near-black charcoal single-logical-pixel outline #171B22 around the exterior bowl/brow/back guard; retain only 5 flat steel/leather material colors #323D4D #4E5D6F #75889B #9FB0BF #5A3A27. All color areas are hard square large connected pixel blocks at a logical 32x48 resolution. No dithering, tiny bright dots, new details, shine stripes, smooth shading or glow.
Preserve the original 1024x1536 whole canvas and transparent padding. Face opening and surroundings remain TRUE alpha zero. Empty equipment only, no skin, face, eyes, hair, body, mannequin, background, text, checkerboard or extra equipment.
assets.refinementReason: Remove the isolated image-left front strips below the brow without changing the steel bowl or face aperture.
assets.revisionReason: Replace checkerboard highlights with connected steel color clusters, remove dangling front fragments, shorten the rear ear guard and preserve the transparent face opening.

sampling.colorDistance: squared RGB distance; each opaque source pixel votes for its nearest palette entry, weighted by overlap area with the target pixel
